title: ICARUS releases ‘Surviving VFR into IMC’ training syllabus
summary: The syllabus leverages the ICARUS Device’s simulator-like capabilities.
body_markdown:
ICARUS Devices has announced the release of its Surviving VFR into IMC training syllabus and is sharing another success story.


The training syllabus fits into the three hours of simulated instrument meteorological conditions (IMC) required for a private pilot airplane rating or the five hours required for a commercial helicopter rating.


The syllabus leverages the ICARUS Device’s simulator-like capabilities and provides instructors with key points to emphasize, recovery techniques, and sample maneuvers to practice.


In this limited instructional time, the goal is to ensure that visual flight rules (VFR) only pilots can both avoid and survive an encounter with bad weather. Too often this training is just an intro to instrument flight rules (IFR).


Syllabus exercises give new pilots visibility benchmarks by demonstrating what marginal conditions look like so that they can both set limits and recognize them. The syllabus utilizes the ICARUS Device’s ability to accurately simulate VFR into IMC to ensure that the startle effect does not lead to a loss of aircraft control.


The key is bringing the simulator’s ability to replicate the sudden loss of visual cues together with the inner ear sensations of actual flight.


[The latest ICARUS success story includes an interview with a pilot who successfully recovered the aircraft when she unexpectedly encountered IMC.](https://youtu.be/iSA0Dvv5rl4) Luckily the pilot had been well trained at Michigan Helicopters, an early adopter of the ICARUS Device. She describes how the good training prepared her for the situation and helped her get out of IMC safely.


ICARUS is a smart view limiting device that allows instructor pilots to simulate IMC or poor visibility *in the aircraft* for dynamic scenario-based training.


ICARUS changes visibility and allows instructor pilots to dial in the visibility for dynamic scenario-based training. Bringing together the controllability of a simulator with the real sensation of flight allows ICARUS to give pilots the best training possible for VFR into IMC, IFR, and weather decision making.


ICARUS has also seen widespread adoption across the aviation spectrum and is flying on all seven continents.[The VFR into IMC Syllabus is available for download on ICARUSDevices.com.](https://icarusdevices.com/resources/) The ICARUS device is made in the USA, priced at $1,250, and comes with a three-year warranty.


*This press release was prepared and distributed by ICARUS Devices.*
